newsitem.title: INDIA: CRICKET-INDIA BEAT AUSTRALIA IN CLIFF-HANGER.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-INDIA BEAT AUSTRALIA IN CLIFF-HANGER.

text.p: Leg-spinner Anil Kumble
bowled India to a thrilling five-run victory over Australia on
Sunday to secure his side a place in the final of the Titan Cup
triangular limited-over series.
Kumble, who had claimed the key wicket of skipper Mark
Taylor in his first spell, returned to clean bowl Paul Reiffel
and Jason Gillespie and apply the brakes as Australia chased
India's imposing 289 for six in 50 overs.
Australia needed six to win from the final over bowled by
Sachin Tendulkar but Brad Hogg was run out at the non-striker's
end off the first ball in a scramble for a leg-bye.
India, with five points from six matches, will now meet
South Africa in Wednesday's final.
"It was an incredible win," Indian skipper Tendulkar said
after the match. "Azharuddin played a fabulous knock to set us
on the victory course and I'm glad we made it."
Australian skipper Taylor said he was disappointed at losing
the match after coming so close to a win.
"(Ian) Healy's run-out was the turning point but on the
whole we batted with aggression," he said.
The Indian innings revolved around Azharuddin's 104-ball
knock of 94 which earned him the man-of-the match award and
Tendulkar's 62 off 61 deliveries after being put in to bat.
Taylor and Mark Waugh launched the Australian run chase on a
rousing note and they were going smoothly until Robin Singh
rattled them with two wickets off successive balls.
Singh bowled Mark Waugh through bat and pad and Stuart Law
then hit his first ball straight to Azharuddin at short
mid-wicket.
Steve Waugh restored order with 33 off 40 balls and Michael
Bevan and Michael Slater threatened to run away with the game
during their 86-run fifth-wicket partnership from 73 balls but
their dismissal in quick succession exposed the Australian tail.
